context.why: The feature is built and every story is accepted. What remains is the writing that makes it findable and understandable by someone who was not here: the project's glossary, its roadmap, and a page the assessment team can actually follow. This is not a tidy-up. The glossary currently defines two roles under names the code no longer uses, and the roadmap still contains a deliverable this feature deliberately superseded, so both describe a portal that no longer exists.
context.environment: Python 3.13 via Poetry, virtualenv already synced. Prefix commands with `poetry run`. Tests: `poetry run pytest`. Lint gate: `poetry run pre-commit run -a`, never raw ruff. A development server is already running from this worktree on 0.0.0.0:8001 with the autoreloader; do not start another and do not stop it.
spec_sections: spec.md in full, as the description of what was built
spec.md Dependencies and risks (the outdated template)
plan_sections: decisions.md D1, D2, D3 and D27
progress.md, which records what each story actually delivered
prior_decisions: D3: CONTEXT.md adopts Data Assessor and Data Curator and retires 'Reviewer' and 'data administrator'. Its own rule is that definitions describe the code as it stands. Keep its rule against writing 'review' unqualified.

D1 and D2: R6 is delivered. R7 narrows to contribution from outside the assessment team, and its deliverable placing team members outside the gate is superseded — a curator's upload does not wait, an assessor's does.

A document is edited to read as current state. No strikethrough over superseded wording, no dated revision stamps, no 'formerly known as'. Git records when each line changed. Clean that pattern out of any section you are already editing, not just out of your own additions.

The distributed upload template still carries two misspelled column headings the portal refuses, so a real file is refused on its header until the template is corrected upstream. The guide must say so plainly — it is the first thing the team will hit.
No internal process vocabulary in any of these files. Write what the software does, for the people who use it.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given CONTEXT.md, When its workflow section is read, Then Data Assessor and Data Curator are defined, the terms they replace are gone rather than annotated, and the rule against writing 'review' unqualified still stands.

Given docs/ROADMAP.md, When R6 and R7 are read, Then R6 reads as delivered, R7 covers only contribution from outside the assessment team, and nothing in either contradicts what was built. No strikethrough and no revision stamps.

Given docs/guides/, When a member of the assessment team reads the new page, Then it covers what each role may do, how to describe an assessment, what a failing file's report means and what to do about it, and states plainly that a file produced from today's template is refused on its header until the template is corrected.
Given the documentation test suite and the repository's documentation check, When both run, Then both are green.

verified_base.note: Full suite green run serially: 908 passed, 1 skipped, 13 xfailed in about 107 seconds. The lint gate is `poetry run pre-commit run -a` and it is clean. If anything is red when you arrive, STOP and report.

rituals: Read specs/005-assessment-upload-workflow/spec.md and progress.md — together they describe exactly what was built, story by story.
Read CONTEXT.md in full before editing it, including its two rules about how it is written.
Read docs/ROADMAP.md R6 and R7, and decisions.md D1 and D2, before rewriting either item.
Read the existing pages under docs/guides/ so the new one matches their voice and structure.
Confirm HEAD equals the verified_base commit before starting.
prohibitions: Stage explicit paths only. Never `git add -A` or `git add .` — this worktree is shared with a running development server and the orchestrator.
Do not stop, restart or start a development server.
Do not change any Python code. This is documentation and vocabulary only. If you find a code defect, report it rather than fixing it.
Never use strikethrough, 'formerly', 'previously known as', or a dated revision stamp. Edit the text to read as current state.
Do not write internal process vocabulary into any of these files.
Do not add any new dependency.
Do not push, open pull requests or comment on GitHub. Commit locally only.
